food and drink practices are important to tourists in negotiating their experiences in destinations, as these practices mediate feelings and emotions, memories, and encounters with others.
food and drink-related activities can be used to negotiate tourists’ experiences of place.
tourists use food and drink practices to establish familiarity with a place and its inhabitants, to create sociability with others, and to construct new feelings of ‘home’.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how food and drink are experienced in tourism and how they contribute to the construction of places.
the ways in which food and drink practices are used by tourists to negotiate their experiences in places.

how tourists’ practices are negotiated in relation to food and drink, and how these practices are experienced in destinations, as a result of their interaction with other tourists, local people and the physical environment.

food and drink-related experiences are important for the negotiation of home and away in destinations.
food and drink-related activities are an important means for tourists to construct their experiences of place.
the study of food and drink is important to understand the experiences of tourists.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
food is a key element in tourists’ experience of place and that it is through the consumption of food that tourists are able to construct a sense of place.
tourists negotiate place and identity through food and drink, but also through the social interactions that are facilitated by food and drink.
tourists use food and drink to negotiate their experiences in places.
The main takeaway from our work is that
food and drink practices are central in mediating tourist experiences, but they are not necessarily experienced in the same way as in everyday life.
food and drink practices can be used as a tool to understand the complex ways in which people negotiate place, and how they experience place through food and drinks.
